messages.author: b8c77fa5305c80cb
messages.subject: surpressing warnings the right way
parts:
Hi,
I am using foreach and doSNOW packages to do some basic parallel processing (and running it from rscript if it is important).
I load them by using:
library(foreach,quietly=TRUE);
library(doSNOW,quietly=TRUE);


The problem is that I get the following warnings:
Warning message:
package 'foreach' was built under R version 3.0.2
Warning message:
package 'doSNOW' was built under R version 3.0.2

which is distracting.
I wanted to disable these warning for the library call (i.e. I still want to get warnings from everything else) but still get an error if no one installed the library for example.
So I tried the following (which I found in http://romainfrancois.blog.free.fr/index.php?post/2009/05/20/Disable-specific-warnings):
suppressWarnings( library(foreach, quietly=TRUE) )

and 

h <- function(w){
    print(w);
    if( any( grepl( "was built under R version", w))) invokeRestart( "muffleWarning" )  
} 
withCallingHandlers( library(foreach,quietly=TRUE), warning = h )

In both cases it indeed suppressed the warning but added
foreach: simple, scalable parallel programming from Revolution Analytics
Use Revolution R for scalability, fault tolerance and more.
http://www.revolutionanalytics.com

I am looking for a way to have it print no messages for these specific calls UNLESS there is a real error and without affecting everything else in the r script.
Thanks,
Assaf.

package 'doSNOW' was built under R version 3.0.2

which is distracting.

So I tried the following (which I found in http://romainfrancois.blog.free.fr/index.php?post/2009/05/20/Disable-specific-warnings):
suppressWarnings( library(foreach, quietly=TRUE) )

and 

h <- function(w){
    print(w);
    if( any( grepl( "was built under R version", w))) invokeRestart( "muffleWarning" )  







} 
withCallingHandlers( library(foreach,quietly=TRUE), warning = h )

In both cases it indeed suppressed the warning but added
foreach: simple, scalable parallel programming from Revolution Analytics
Use Revolution R for scalability, fault tolerance and more.
http://www.revolutionanalytics.com

I am looking for a way to have it print no messages for these specific calls UNLESS there is a real error and without affecting everything else in the r script.
Thanks,
Assaf.

messages.subject: Re: [Israel RUG] surpressing warnings the right way
parts:
By reading the source of library() I learned that library ultimately invokes message(). 
message() sends output to the stderr so you would expect sink(type="message") to capture them.

Nevertheless, that brought be to the informatively named suppressPackageStartupMessages() function and suppressMessages() which should do what you want.

yeah, that is what I mean changed. If I try any of the options to suppress the warnings then it ignores the fact that I do quietly=TRUE and prints the message. If I do not mess with the warnings then it respects the quietly but gives the  package was build with... warning

The library() function has a quitely= argument. Its default is FALSE.
Did you try that?

in both
